challenge: An agent must decide whether a thing already exists before building it. Existence was checked with ad hoc globs whose coverage was never stated, so a search that could not have found the target was indistinguishable from one that found nothing.
observedFailure: Eight artefacts were reported as not existing in one session. All eight existed. The probe covered depth one; node-platform sits at depth two. It returned zero matches and exit code zero. Two of the eight were the nodeplatform.repo-contract ownership entry and evt:copy-as-proof-surface, the latter already promoted with evidence and a derived invariant.
resolution: Added scripts/recall.mjs, which reads nine roots across both halves with no depth limit and has no code path that prints absent. It returns matches, or exactly what it read: every root, whether it existed, how many files were opened, which were unreadable. On its first execution it caught its own defect, reporting seven roots MISSING because import.meta.url percent-encoded a space, rather than reporting the target as not found.
knownLimitations: interpretation.status is a const of "human-reviewed" with no value for an agent-authored record, so this field asserts a review that has not happened. The drafts/ directory is the only real not-canonical signal. Do not read the status field as approval.
Proves what was read, never that a thing does not exist. Absence remains unprovable by search.
Substring matching only. A decision recorded in different words is not found.
The root list is fixed in source. A store not in that list is invisible — the original failure at a different scale.
ChatGPT threads are not a root; the reasoning half is covered only by local memory and skills.
